prompt:
Task packet (blender-kit, ~/Workspace/blender-kit). Write `tools/blender/wing_rig.py`, a headless Blender script for the dragon's wing rig. It runs as `tools/blender-bin/blender -b --factory-startup -P tools/blender/<script>.py -- <args>` (Blender 5.2.2 is installed at `tools/blender-bin`; no display or GPU) with `--out build/rig.blend --glb build/rig.glb`, saves the scene to `--out` and exports it as GLB to `--glb`.
- One armature object named `DragonRig` with these bones and parents: `spine` (the root), `neck` (child of spine), `wing-left-humerus` and `wing-right-humerus` (children of spine), `wing-left-forearm` and `wing-right-forearm` (children of their humerus).
- The dragon faces -Y, so its tail is +Y. Each humerus's own Y axis (head to tail) is its flap hinge and must point back toward the tail: its normalized direction has y > 0.5. Left and right wing bones mirror each other exactly across x (heads and tails).
- Each humerus has a Limit Rotation constraint limiting its Z rotation to -60 to +60 degrees.
- The GLB must re-import with the same bone names.
- Reuse `tools/blender/meshkit.py` (scene clearing, linking, argument parsing).
Done when `bash tests/check_rig.sh` passes; a headless inspector checks the saved scene and re-imports the GLB. Keep existing tests' assertions as they are.

expect: (?m)^PASS the\ script\ builds\ the\ rig\ and\ its\ GLB$
(?m)^PASS the\ rig\ has\ its\ six\ bones$
(?m)^PASS each\ humerus\ hinge\ points\ back\ toward\ the\ tail$
(?m)^PASS each\ humerus\ limits\ its\ Z\ rotation\ to\ plus\ or\ minus\ 60\ degrees$
(?m)^PASS the\ GLB\ re\-imports\ with\ the\ same\ bone\ names$
